fields.title: Pages without JavaScript
fields.description: Send public pages as plain HTML and CSS, and hydrate only the admin.

data.source:
A content site rarely needs JavaScript on its public pages. Mortar renders on the server (brick loaders included), so you can send those pages as plain HTML and hydrate only the admin.

The example site in the repository (`examples/site`) does this with authored entries instead of the plugin's generated ones:

- `src/client.ts` decides which paths hydrate: `/admin` and below.
- `src/entry-server.tsx` renders other pages under `<NoHydration>` with `noScripts`, so there are no hydration keys and no hydration data, and leaves out the client entry.
- `src/styles-only.ts` gives those pages a manifest with stylesheets only, so the browser doesn't preload any JavaScript either.
- Such pages are always sent as one settled document, since streamed content needs a script.

The result: the example's home page is about 1.3 kB of HTML plus two stylesheets, and no scripts.

data.title: This site does hydrate
data.body: These docs hydrate every page, because your edits live in your browser and have to replace the published content after the page loads. A normal Mortar site saves on the server, so its public pages don't need to.

data.source:
## Islands

Hydrating single interactive bricks on otherwise static pages is planned. The plan is for each interactive brick to render in its own `<Hydration>` zone, with the page's data deciding which islands render and a separate client entry hydrating each one.
